newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed in quiet trading.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mixed on Thursday in subdued dealings as several dealers opted to stay on the sidelines ahead the November 12 U.S. Department of Agriculture crop report.
"I think everybody is watching the CBOT corn board go up and see if (prices) are for real, wait a bit until the crop report comes out next Tuesday and then make a decision," a dealer said.
"Nearby sales for this week and next week is the only thing trading. Nobody is looking for anything forward," one Texas dealer said.

One Minnesota broker noted a reluctance to lock in at current prices. "You (the buyer) are not risking a lot by not covering needs because you are not going to pay a whole lot more. You could pay less, so why buy now," he said.
But he said the onslaught of cold weather should improve consumption. "It takes more feed to keep the animal warm and there are also no pastures. Therefore demand should pick up," he said.
But a Buffalo dealer said mills in the northeast have been running a little short but this weekend some mills will be running.
"At least we have something to sell here," he said.
